title: Middleware and one place for errors

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where requests pass Hesper's middleware and errors go to one place.

tasks.title: Run middleware before the handler
tasks.description:
Implement `use(router, fn)` in `src/router.js`, and run middleware in `handle`.

- `use` adds a middleware, a function `fn(req, res, next)`; it throws a `TypeError` when `fn` is not a function
- for a request that reaches a route, after its params, query and body are ready, every middleware runs in the order it was added, then the handler
- calling `next()` goes on to the next middleware, or to the handler after the last one; a middleware may call it later, after an `await`
- `next()` returns a promise that settles once the rest of the chain has finished, so `await next()` comes back after the handler
- a middleware that answers without calling `next()` ends the request: nothing after it runs
- `handle` finishes only once the whole chain has, an async handler included
- a request the router answers by itself, a 404, a 405, or a path or body it cannot take, runs no middleware

The check adds middleware of its own that notes when it runs, and reads the order.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and read the error.
Keep each middleware on the router in `use`.
In `handle`, make a list of the middleware followed by the handler, and write a function that runs step `i` and gives it a `next` that runs step `i + 1`.
Return the promise of the rest from `next`, and wait for the first step in `handle`.
hints: The chain is not a loop. Each step decides whether the next one runs, by calling `next` or not, so the next step has to start from inside `next`.
An `async` function that runs step `i` returns a promise. If `next` returns `runStep(i + 1)`, that promise settles when everything after step `i` has finished.
`async function runStep(i) { await chain[i](req, res, () => runStep(i + 1)) }`, and in `handle`, `await runStep(0)`. The last step is the handler.

tasks.title: Hand errors to one place
tasks.description:
Implement `onError(router, fn)` in `src/router.js`, and send every error from the chain there.

- `onError` sets the router's error handler, a function `fn(error, req, res)` that answers
- `next(error)`, a throw, or a promise that rejects, in a middleware or in the handler, skips everything left in the chain and calls the error handler once, with that very error
- with no error handler, the router answers `500` with `{ error }`; the same when the error handler itself throws
- that `{ error }` never contains the error's own message: it says that something went wrong, in your words

The check throws one error from different places, and notes what the error handler gets and what the answer says.
nextSteps: Keep the error handler on the router in `onError`.
Make `next(error)` stop the chain with that error.
Wrap the run of the chain in `handle` in a `try`, and hand what you catch to the error handler.
Think about what happens when the error handler throws too.
hints: If every error, wherever it starts, ends up as a rejected promise of the chain, one `try` around the chain in `handle` catches them all.
`await` turns a rejected promise into a throw, and a throw inside an `async` function into a rejected promise. `next(error)` can return `Promise.reject(error)`.
`try { await runStep(0) } catch (error) { ... router's error handler(error, req, res) ... }`, with a second `try` around the error handler and a plain 500 when there is none.

tasks.title: Never leave a request hanging
tasks.description:
Make `handle` notice a step that finished without doing its job, and say which one.

- a step has finished when its function returned, or when the promise it returned settled
- a middleware that finished without answering and without calling `next()` is answered `500` with `{ error }` that names it: `middleware 2` for the second one added, counted from 1
- a handler that finished without answering is answered `500` with `{ error }` that names its route by method and pattern, such as `GET /orders/:id`
- a step that answered has done its job, whether or not it called `next()`
- calling `next()` a second time does nothing

The check adds middleware and handlers that forget their job, and reads the answer.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and look at the proof request.
After a step has finished, look at two things: was `next` called, and has the response ended?
Give every step a name you can put in the answer.
Make `next` remember that it was called, and do nothing the second time.
hints: A step that neither answers nor calls `next` leaves a client waiting for ever. The router is the only one that can see it happen, because it knows when each step finished.
`res.writableEnded` is true once the response has ended. Look at it after the step's promise has settled, not straight after the call.
In `runStep`, after `await fn(req, res, next)`: `if (!calledNext && !res.writableEnded)` throw an error that says which step it was, and answer it with a 500 in `handle`.
